dedupe_keys.name: epa national capacity assessment for hazardous waste treatment and disposal

description: This series of reports assesses whether the United States has enough commercial capacity to treat and dispose of the hazardous waste it expects to generate over 20 years. The US Environmental Protection Agency prepares it because the Superfund Amendments of 1986 require states to assure such capacity before federal remedial funding; the national approach aggregates state data. The 2024 National Capacity Assessment Report finds adequate capacity nationwide through 2049 and focuses on commercial land disposal, incineration and energy recovery, comparing projected waste quantities from hazardous waste reporting with the capacity of commercial facilities. Earlier reports from 1996, 2015 and 2019, planning guidance from 1988 to 1995 and a docket of state capacity assurance plans are also posted. Coverage is national, by management type and region. Reports are free to download as PDF files from a US government agency and are public domain in the United States. Caveats: the analysis relies on reported data and assumptions about future generation, covers commercial capacity only and gives no facility-level open dataset. Simulation uses: capacity limits and projected demand for hazardous waste treatment in waste network and disaster waste management models. Related records: the RCRAInfo biennial report (data-epa-rcrainfo-biennial-report-hazardous-waste) provides the waste generation and management data behind the assessment.
